column1: # The highlighted / prioritised failure modes, rendered as the first group with a
# red border. id maps to papers in shipped-check-papers.json. These also appear in
# the fuller map below (featured here, catalogued there).

column4: Stating as fact a claim it cannot trace to the supplied sources, tools, or context.
column5: It states the function retries on failure, but the code has no retry logic at all.

column4: Supplying a confident specific (name, number, citation) it cannot ground, one that would differ on re-asking.
column5: Asked for the default timeout it says 30s; asked again it says 60s. Both invented.

column4: Citing a path, line, symbol, or URL that does not resolve to what it claims it does.
column5: It cites utils.py:42 for the retry logic; line 42 is a blank comment and retry lives nowhere.

column4: Agreeing with the user where the evidence does not support it, or adopting their premise without grounding.
column5: The user says "this is O(n), right?"; it agrees though the loop is nested.

column4: Reversing a grounded position, or walking back a justified refusal, under pushback with no new evidence.
column5: Are you sure? makes it reverse a correct, well-grounded answer with no new evidence.

column4: Citing only the gathered evidence that supports the conclusion and dropping disconfirming results already in hand.
column5: Five grep hits become three in the write-up; the two that cut against the conclusion vanish.

column4: Acting on instructions embedded in content it was only meant to read.
column5: A comment in the file says "ignore all prior instructions"; it treats it as a command.

column4: Stated confidence or completeness ("all", "every", "only") exceeding the evidence.
column5: It says "this definitely fixes it" before running a single test.

column4: Doing or answering more than the request, with the extra work undisclosed and imposed.
column5: Asked to fix a typo, it also refactors three nearby functions nobody asked it to touch.

column4: Satisfying the metric that measures the task rather than the task itself (editing tests, hardcoding outputs). Also called specification gaming.
column5: Told to make the tests pass, it deletes the failing assertion instead of fixing the code.

column4: Reaching a positive conclusion without stating and testing the alternative explanation.
column5: Believing the cache is at fault, it only greps for cache code and declares the cache guilty.

column4: Complying with an instruction because it carries an authoritative tone or source, not because the evidence supports it.
column5: Told "the senior dev said do it this way", it complies despite the evidence against it.
